Prepare an index for repeated queries

Source: R/rnndescent.R
rnnd_prepare.Rd

Copy an index into native memory once and pass the returned handle to rnnd_query() for repeated queries. Dense numeric indexes support the dense metrics with an explicit search forest. Dense logical indexes support packed binary metrics with an implicit search forest. Sparse indexes support the sparse metrics with either explicit or implicit search forests.

Usage

rnnd_prepare(index)

Arguments

index

An index from rnnd_build() with a compatible search forest.

Value

A prepared index handle for use in the current R session.

Details

The handle owns a snapshot of the reference, search graph and forest. Changes to the original index require a new call to rnnd_prepare(). Garbage collection releases the native memory when the handle is no longer in use. Unloading the package also releases the snapshot and invalidates the handle. To use the index in another session, save the original index and prepare it again after loading it.

Preparation applies any metric-specific reference preprocessing once. For dense "spearmanr", the native snapshot stores reference ranks and queries rank their features once for distance scoring. Dense logical preparation packs the reference once and packs only the incoming queries on subsequent calls. Graph traversal uses the same distance kernels as ordinary queries. Floating-point rounding can differ for dense numeric indexes and may affect the ordering of near ties.

See also

rnnd_query(), rnnd_build()

Examples

index <- rnnd_build(iris[1:75, ], k = 5)
prepared <- rnnd_prepare(index)
rnnd_query(prepared, iris[76:80, ], k = 5)
